text: aren’t Philippines-specific – ’re handy building blocks fake dataset. Two worth closer look: fkr_multiple_response() pretends survey question someone can pick one answer (“select apply” question): fkr_factor() creates fake category column, code friendlier label attached – similar survey statistics software lets store 1/2 display “Male”/“Female”: can also attach short description whole column (value) using label:

title: Generate ages — fkr_age
text: Draws n ages age_range, weighted exponential decay , like real population pyramid, younger ages common older ones default.

title: Generate ages — fkr_age
text: n Number ages generate. single non-negative whole number. age_range Integer vector candidate ages. Default 0:130. values must non-negative. bias Exponential decay rate applied age_range (exp(bias * age)). Negative values (default, -0.05) make younger ages likely; 0 makes every age age_range equally likely; positive values make older ages likely.

what: Generate a factor variable with value labels and an optional variable label — fkr_factor
title: Generate a factor variable with value labels and an optional variable label — fkr_factor
text: Draws values (underlying, often numeric, codes) returns factor() , optionally relabeled human-readable labels (value set) tagged label (variable-level description), mirroring "variable label" / "value labels" distinction common survey/statistical data (e.g. SPSS, Stata, haven).

title: Generate a factor variable with value labels and an optional variable label — fkr_factor
code: fkr_factor(n, values, labels = NULL, label = NULL, prob = NULL)

title: Generate a factor variable with value labels and an optional variable label — fkr_factor
text: n Number values generate. single non-negative whole number. values non-empty atomic vector underlying codes/levels, NAs (e.g. c(1, 2) c("M", "F")). labels Optional character vector display labels, length values order (e.g. c("Male", "Female") values = c(1, 2)). NULL (default), values used labels, plain factor(). label Optional single string describing variable (e.g. "Respondent's biological sex"), attached attr(x, "label") – confused labels, per-value display text. prob Optional numeric vector sampling weights, length values. Default NULL draws every value equal probability.

title: Generate a factor variable with value labels and an optional variable label — fkr_factor
text: factor length n levels values (coerced character, per factor()'s usual behavior) , given, attr(x, "label") variable description. Note .integer() result gives value's position values, original code – use levels() .character() recover original values.

title: Generate a factor variable with value labels and an optional variable label — fkr_factor
code: fkr_factor(5, values = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female")) #> [1] Male   Male   Male   Female Male   #> Levels: Male Female fkr_factor(5,   values = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"),   label = "Respondent's biological sex" ) #> [1] Female Female Female Female Female #> attr(,"label") #> [1] Respondent's biological sex #> Levels: Male Female fkr_factor(5, values = c(1, 2, 3), prob = c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1)) #> [1] 1 1 1 1 1 #> Levels: 1 2 3

title: Generate multiple-response (select-all-that-apply) values — fkr_multiple_response
text: Simulates "select apply" survey item: generated value one entries values combined together, e.g. values = LETTERS[1:4] result might "", "AC", "ABCD". Selected entries always keep original order values ("AC" can occur "CA" ), never repeat within single generated value.

title: Generate multiple-response (select-all-that-apply) values — fkr_multiple_response
text: n Number values generate. single non-negative whole number. values non-empty vector candidate entries, NAs, combine (e.g. LETTERS[1:4], option labels like c("Email", "Phone", "SMS")). multiple TRUE (default), generated value may combine one entry values. FALSE, exactly one entry drawn per value, single-response ("select one") item. sep String used join multiple selected entries together. Default "", reads naturally values single characters (e.g. "AC"); multi-character values, pass something like sep = ", " keep entries distinguishable (e.g. "Email, SMS").

title: Generate multiple-response (select-all-that-apply) values — fkr_multiple_response
text: character vector length n.

title: Generate multiple-response (select-all-that-apply) values — fkr_multiple_response
text: number entries selected value drawn uniformly 1:length(values) (uniformly non-empty subsets), picking exactly 1 entry just likely picking .

title: Generate multiple-response (select-all-that-apply) values — fkr_multiple_response
code: fkr_multiple_response(5, values = LETTERS[1:4]) #> [1] "ABC" "C"   "BD"  "ABC" "D"   fkr_multiple_response(5, values = c("Email", "Phone", "SMS"), sep = ", ") #> [1] "Email, Phone" "Email"        "SMS"          "Email, Phone" "SMS"          fkr_multiple_response(5, values = LETTERS[1:4], multiple = FALSE) #> [1] "A" "B" "A" "A" "C"
